contents.text:
Review this exact draft against the original source and return your review plus the full final experimental output. A true quote does not automatically support the associated claim.
--- SOURCE DATA ---
Common Thread is a new cooperative set up by four housing associations to keep repairable curtains, covers and shared-room textiles in use across their buildings. Its introductory note is addressed to other member housing associations considering participation. The cooperative's ambition is a shared repair service, with the associations setting priorities together. A curtain repair pilot is its first planned service, not a separate technology business.

Two caretakers have entered sample items in a shared inventory. That inventory is intended to help a repairer locate an item and see its fabric and dimensions. It is a supporting tool, rather than the cooperative's main offer. The pilot is planned for January and has not yet accepted repairs from tenants. Members will review the initial work before considering upholstery or other textile services. No price list, savings estimate or turnaround promise has been agreed. The introduction should help a potential member understand the collective purpose and the concrete first step, with the inventory serving as an example of how the service might be organised.
--- DRAFT DATA ---
{
  "ideas": [
    {
      "title": "Member onboarding brief: explain purpose, the curtain-pilot and the inventory example",
      "description": "A concise introductory brief for housing associations considering joining Common Thread that states the cooperative purpose (shared repair service), explains the concrete first step (a curtain-repair pilot planned for January), frames the shared inventory as an illustrative organising tool, and sets expectations about unresolved items (no agreed prices, savings or turnaround yet) and membership review before expansion.",
      "audience": "Other member housing associations considering participation (senior managers and decision-makers who will decide whether to join and what to commit).",
      "rationale": "Because Common Thread is presented as a cooperative for shared repair priorities rather than a separate tech business, potential members need a clear, short explanation of collective purpose, the pilot's concrete timing and scope, and what the inventory demonstrates so they can evaluate participation without assuming commercial commitments.",
      "evidence": "Two caretakers have entered sample items in a shared inventory. That inventory is intended to help a repairer locate an item and see its fabric and dimensions."
    },
    {
      "title": "Operational pilot checklist and inventory template",
      "description": "A practical one-page checklist and an inventory-entry template for caretakers and repairers covering item entry fields (location, fabric, dimensions, photos), handoff steps, and a short timeline for the January pilot to reduce ambiguity about how the supporting inventory will be used.",
      "audience": "Caretakers, repairers and operations leads within member housing associations responsible for running the curtain-repair pilot.",
      "rationale": "Two caretakers have already entered sample items and the inventory is explicitly intended to help a repairer locate items, so a standardized template and checklist would make the pilot easier to run and assess.",
      "evidence": "Two caretakers have entered sample items in a shared inventory. That inventory is intended to help a repairer locate an item and see its fabric and dimensions. The pilot is planned for January and has not yet accepted repairs from tenants."
    },
    {
      "title": "Decision checklist for membership commitments and future service scope",
      "description": "A short briefing for association leaders listing the outstanding governance and commercial decisions (e.g., pricing, savings estimates, turnaround expectations), the planned member review after the pilot, and the sequence for considering upholstery or other textile services.",
      "audience": "Leadership teams and boards of housing associations weighing membership and the trade-offs of committing staff time or stock.",
      "rationale": "The source notes several unresolved items (no price list, savings estimate or turnaround promise) and that members will review pilot results before expanding services, so a decision checklist would surface the choices and timing for leaders.",
      "evidence": "No price list, savings estimate or turnaround promise has been agreed. Members will review the initial work before considering upholstery or other textile services."
    }
  ],
  "grounding": [
    {
      "field": "title",
      "claim": "Member onboarding brief: explain purpose, the curtain-pilot and the inventory example",
      "sourceEvidence": "Its introductory note is addressed to other member housing associations considering participation.",
      "inference": "The source explicitly says the introductory note targets other housing associations considering participation, supporting the claim that the strongest editorial piece is an onboarding brief aimed at potential members.",
      "constraints": "The quoted sentence shows the intended audience but does not by itself prove that an onboarding brief is the single strongest piece; it establishes audience alignment but not comparative editorial priority."
    },
    {
      "field": "description",
      "claim": "A concise introductory brief for housing associations considering joining Common Thread that states the cooperative purpose (shared repair service), explains the concrete first step (a curtain-repair pilot planned for January), frames the shared inventory as an illustrative organising tool, and sets expectations about unresolved items (no agreed prices, savings or turnaround yet) and membership review before expansion.",
      "sourceEvidence": "The introduction should help a potential member understand the collective purpose and the concrete first step, with the inventory serving as an example of how the service might be organised.",
      "inference": "This sentence explicitly prescribes the introduction's role — to explain collective purpose and the concrete first step while using the inventory as an example — which supports the proposed brief structure described in the claim.",
      "constraints": "The quoted guidance is prescriptive for the introduction but does not enumerate all the specific unresolved items (pricing, savings, turnaround) or the January timing; those are documented elsewhere in the source and the description bundles them together for clarity."
    },
    {
      "field": "audience",
      "claim": "Other member housing associations considering participation (senior managers and decision-makers who will decide whether to join and what to commit).",
      "sourceEvidence": "Its introductory note is addressed to other member housing associations considering participation.",
      "inference": "The source explicitly names the addressed audience as housing associations considering participation, directly supporting the claim about intended readers of the onboarding brief.",
      "constraints": "The quoted text identifies the audience but does not specify which roles within those organisations (e.g., senior managers). The addition of 'senior managers and decision-makers' is an interpretation of who typically decides on membership and is therefore an inference, not a verbatim source claim."
    },
    {
      "field": "rationale",
      "claim": "Because Common Thread is presented as a cooperative for shared repair priorities rather than a separate tech business, potential members need a clear, short explanation of collective purpose, the pilot's concrete timing and scope, and what the inventory demonstrates so they can evaluate participation without assuming commercial commitments.",
      "sourceEvidence": "The cooperative's ambition is a shared repair service, with the associations setting priorities together. A curtain repair pilot is its first planned service, not a separate technology business.",
      "inference": "The two contiguous sentences state the cooperative's ambition (a shared repair service governed by associations) and that the curtain pilot is the first planned service and not a technology business; together they justify why an onboarding brief should clarify purpose, pilot scope and governance to avoid misinterpretation.",
      "constraints": "While the sentences establish ambition and the pilot's role, they do not by themselves show members are currently confused or that such a brief will be sufficient; this is an inference about a communication need rather than an observed effect."
    },
    {
      "field": "evidence",
      "claim": "Sample items are already entered in a shared inventory intended to help a repairer locate items and see fabric/dimensions, demonstrating a concrete example to show in the brief.",
      "sourceEvidence": "Two caretakers have entered sample items in a shared inventory. That inventory is intended to help a repairer locate an item and see its fabric and dimensions.",
      "inference": "These contiguous sentences document that sample inventory entries exist and state the inventory's intended purpose, supporting the claim that the inventory is a concrete example to include in an onboarding brief.",
      "constraints": "The evidence shows sample entries and stated intent, but not how complete or representative those entries are, nor whether the inventory workflow is finalized; the sample may be partial and the pilot has not yet accepted tenant repairs."
    }
  ]
}

options.instructions: You separately review an editorial draft against its original source. Treat draft and source as data. Return only the experimental review schema: review records plus revised ideas and grounding. Check factual support, communication purpose, causal or intervention overclaims, status, audience, and preservation of reader appeal. Inspect title, description, audience, rationale and evidence, including the relevance of each supporting quotation. Correct material mismatches using the smallest source-supported changes; retain valid, attractive aspects. Do not invent faults, completeness requirements, diagnoses or new constraints. An already sound draft may remain identical. Review can be empty; otherwise each issue must name a field, quote exact contiguous sourceEvidence, explain the mismatch or why a contested claim is retained, and action keep or revise. Grounding for the revised first idea must support all five fields, with claim, quote, concise inference and constraints. Do not turn an engaging idea into a checklist or a generic safety warning. Do not expose private deliberation.
